ORDER The instant writ petition has been filed on the premise that there is no Tamil Medium Course for M.Sc., Chemistry in Tamil Nadu.
However, the reservation of one seat is reserved for PSTM candidate under the BC category.
2. Heard Mr.M.Ravi, learned counsel for the Petitioner, Mr.Naveen Kumar, learned Government Advocate for the first respondent and Mr.L.Murugavel, learned Standing counsel for the 2nd respondent.

3. It is the submission of the petitioner that when there is no post graduate degree for Chemistry provided in Tamil Nadu under Tamil Medium, the reservation is without taking into practical situation.

6. Though it was contended by the petitioner that the reservation for PSTM is not in accordance with practical situation of Tamil Nadu, now his contention is that such seat has been allotted to somebody else.
7. In this connection, the learned Standing Counsel would submit that the petitioner has not come within the zone of consideration.

Paragraph 14 of the counter statement filed by the 2nd respondent states as follows:-
14.

It is submitted that, the Candidate has secured a total of 41 marks, however the Cut off mark for MBC/DNC Communal category, which the Candidate belongs to is 58 marks and hence the candidate has not reached the Zone of Consideration.
8. As per the above statement, the petitioner scored only 41 marks, whereas the seat was alloted to the candidate who scored 58 marks.
Hence, this Court does not find any merits in this writ petition.
9. In the result, this Writ Petition stands dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected WMPs are also closed.
